facts.statement: Born at Coate in Wiltshire in 1848; died 1887.
Wrote natural history, rural essays, Bevis (1882), The Story of My Heart (1883) and After London (1885).

interpretation.note: Interpretation of the documented life and works; no claim of personal acquaintance from shared themes.

appraisal.note: AETERNUS editorial judgement; not presented as a historical quotation.

en.tagline: The fields of Wiltshire, and the world beyond them.
en.intro: Jefferies looked closely at a country within walking distance. Fields, hedges, labour and the movement of animals became the materials of a prose that could pass from observation into speculation.
en.orientation: The nature essay is only one part of his work. Bevis imagines childhood’s freedom; After London asks what might follow the collapse of a civilisation.
origin: He grew up at Coate in Wiltshire. The farm and its surrounding countryside supplied a durable store of observation, though his writing continually outgrew a purely local subject.
career: Journalism and essays opened into several literary forms. During his short life he wrote about agriculture and rural society as well as the inward life and imagined futures.
literature: The Story of My Heart is an exploration of inward experience; After London transforms familiar terrain into a strange future. The observer of an English field was also an inventor of worlds.
en.legacy: Jefferies offers an attentive, restless form of nature writing. His local knowledge makes the larger imaginative departures more remarkable.
en.bridge: The books reveal the range between the precisely seen countryside and the landscapes the mind builds from it.
